transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Alvarez (Redwood SE); Marcus Lee (CedarGate CTO), Sara Thompson (Lead ML Eng), Ravi Patel (Security), Tom Wu (DevOps)

Summary: Short walkthrough of Redwood's Model Catalog in the Console, demoing model selection, benchmarks, and the compatibility matrix. Customer asked about latency targets, cost per token, KV cache, quantization compatibility, and private deployment options.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, with Priya and Jordan. How's everybody doing?
[00:08] Marcus: Good thanks, excited to see the model catalog. We're evaluating options for our clinical note summarization pipeline.
[00:14] Alex: Great. Quick agenda: show the Console, pick open models, review benchmark numbers (99th p99, mean latency), and the compatibility matrix for dedicated/private deploys, then Q&A.
[00:30] Priya: I'll share my screen — show the Model Catalog page. One note: some auto-generated names in the transcribe might be off.
[00:38] [screen share noise]
[00:42] Priya: Here we have a curated list of open models — we surface latency and cost profiles per model, and recommended quantization options. For example, we show llama2-13b, mosaicml/galactica-like variants, and some 7B options.
[00:55] Sara: Are these performance numbers from your hosted infra or from customer runs?
[00:59] Priya: Primarily Redwood-hosted benchmarks on the standard workloads, but we also show dedicated results when customers run our benchmark harness on their fleet. You can export the CSV — Jordan will show that.
[01:10] Jordan: Pulling up the benchmark dashboard. You'll see throughput, mean latency, p95/p99, and cost per 1k tokens estimated with dynamic batching. 
[01:22] Ravi: Quick compliance question — do your benchmarks include scenarios with KMS enabled or with encrypted kernels?
[01:28] Priya: Good call. By default our public benchmark numbers are with standard keys, but we annotate whether a run included KMS/HSM or private networking. For private deployments there is a small overhead we measure — typically 3–6% latency increase depending on network topology.
[01:45] Marcus: Our requirement is p99 under 300ms for prompts that are ~60 tokens. Cost is also important — we have 10M tokens/month baseline. How do you recommend selecting a model?
[02:00] Priya: We generally pick the smallest model that meets your quality bar. The Console lets you compare quality vs latency: side-by-side eval scores, prompt set-based regression checks, and the Model Catalog shows recommended quant profiles like FP16 vs int8/q4_0 depending on hardware.
[02:18] Sara: We saw your Optimize suggestions mention batching and KV cache. Does that apply to short chatty prompts? We're concerned caching will not help because the prompts vary a lot.
[02:28] Jordan: KV caching helps mainly for multi-turn chat or reuse of prefixes; for one-off summarization it matters less. But continuous batching and dynamic batching still reduce cost; for small requests it can queue a few requests for 10-30ms windows. We expose those controls in Redwood Optimize.
[02:45] [crosstalk] Tom: If you batch, does that spike latency?
[02:48] Priya: There's a tradeoff — the Console shows expected latency percentiles for different batching windows. For your p99 <300ms target on 60-token prompts, we suggest reserved capacity with small batching windows (10–20ms) and int8 quant where quality holds.
[03:05] Marcus: What about compatibility matrix — I want to ensure model X quantizes to int8 and runs on our A100s vs our on-prem Ampere clones.
[03:14] Priya: Let me pull up the compatibility matrix tab.
[03:17] [screen share noise]
[03:20] Priya: Here's the matrix — rows are model families, columns are runtime/quant options and hardware (T4, A10, A100, H100, CPU with int8). We annotate known issues: for instance, some attentions kernels are not yet optimized for H100 int4 paths so we flag them.
[03:38] Sara: Do you have model-specific fuzz tests or correctness regressions after quant? We're worried about hallucinations after aggressive quantization.
[03:45] Jordan: Yes, we run eval suites tied to your prompt sets. The Console's Evaluate feature can run your prompt set against model+quant config and surface quality deltas. We also have automated rollback if a quality regression exceeds a threshold.
[03:58] Ravi: Security — does Redwood support SSO/SAML, RBAC, and audit logs? And how about auditability for model weights (we have strict sourcing rules).
[04:08] Alex: We support SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, role-based access controls, and per-request audit logs; on Private we integrate with your KMS/HSM. For model sourcing we provide provenance metadata in the catalog (model checkpoints origin, license). We'll share the security whitepaper.
[04:25] Marcus: Regarding deployment, we're leaning toward Dedicated for predictable latency but we might need Private later for PHI. Can you run a POC in our VPC?
[04:35] Priya: Absolutely — we do VPC peering or private link depending on cloud, and for on-prem we provide a Private package. The main differences are: Hosted = fastest onboarding, Dedicated = reserved capacity + SLA, Private = customer-managed network and KMS.
[04:49] Sara: Do you have real numbers for cost per 1k tokens for, say, llama2-13b int8 vs 7b fp16?
[04:56] Jordan: Rough ballpark from recent benchmarks: llama2-13b int8 at our Dedicated config ~ $0.55 per 1k tokens (inference-only), 7b fp16 around $0.22 per 1k tokens. These are estimates — we'll provide the detailed CSV. Also note cost drops with better batching and KV reuse.
[05:16] Tom: Are these numbers including KV cache storage and network egress?
[05:20] Jordan: Egress is separate; KV cache storage is typically negligible vs GPU cost unless you have massive persistent caches. We'll annotate all of that in the exported sheet.
[05:32] Marcus: On latency, 13b int8 p99 was what?
[05:35] Jordan: For 60-token prompts on A100, p99 was around 280–320ms in our shared hosted runs; with Dedicated reserved capacity we got it down to ~260ms in the harness. H100 can be faster but depends on kernel support.
[05:48] Sara: If we run on our A100s on-prem with your Private package, how much integration work is typical?
[05:56] Priya: Usually we run our benchmark harness first — install a lightweight agent, run tests, validate networking and KMS configs. Typical timeline 2–4 weeks for initial POC, depending on procurement and access.
[06:10] Ravi: For compliance we need SOC2, ISO docs and a diagram of where logs and keys live. Also we need SIEM integration — do you push logs to their Splunk or S3?
[06:19] Alex: We can push audit logs to customer S3, and we support syslog/Splunk via connectors. We'll attach SOC2 and ISO attestation docs. On KMS, we support customer KMS for Private and Dedicated; hosted uses Redwood-managed keys unless you enable Bring-Your-Own-Key.
[06:36] [pause, typing]
[06:40] Marcus: One concern — model switching fallback. If you throttle on capacity, can requests fall back to a smaller model without breaking app-level contracts?
[06:49] Priya: Yes, our Smart Routing supports fallbacks by policy. You can define a primary model plus compatible variants; we do automatic type checks and response-length heuristics. For critical flows we recommend canonical safe-fallbacks with monitoring.
[07:02] Sara: Any gotchas with prompt-templating across model families? We had different tokenization effects when switching from 13b to 7b.
[07:10] Jordan: Tokenization differences do exist; Console will run a tokenization preview and flag token count deltas. Our eval harness includes tokenization-normalized metrics.
[07:22] Marcus: Ok that helps. Can you share a compatibility matrix for our particular hardware mix (A100 + some older Ampere clones)?
[07:29] Alex: We'll produce a custom compatibility matrix as part of the POC pack. Priya will take the hardware list.
[07:36] Ravi: Also need data residency notes for EMEA — our clinicians are in the UK, we need logs retained in-region.
[07:43] Alex: We have region controls; for Hosted we can provision region-specific endpoints, Dedicated & Private obviously give you region control.
[07:51] [screen navigate to next tab]
[07:54] Priya: Quick demo of Console export: here's the Benchmark CSV, here's the Model Catalog entry for 'open-llama-13b' with tags: quant-ready, recommended-for-summarization, known-good-on-a100. You can click to run an on-demand eval with your prompt set.
[08:12] Sara: If we run our own prompt set, how long until we see results?
[08:16] Jordan: Depends on size; small sets (hundreds) can run in minutes to an hour; larger scale evaluatons are queued. We'll prioritize trial POC runs.
[08:28] Marcus: Let's talk timelines: procurement is aiming for POC signoff in June.
[08:33] Alex: Sounds doable; we'll get you the pricing and POC docs this week.
[08:38] Ravi: Please include a sample architecture diagram showing where KMS and audit logs are for Private.
[08:43] Alex: Will do.
[08:45] [wrap-up]
[08:46] Alex: Quick recap — action items: share pricing + compatibility matrix + benchmark CSV, schedule POC scoping, share security docs. Any other questions?
[08:55] Marcus: No, thanks — that was very useful.
[09:00] Alex: Great, thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
